subject: history
title: Conquest of the Plains Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace how railroads, homesteaders and soldiers transformed and conquered the Plains.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Homestead Act, Transcontinental Railroad, Plains Wars and Wounded Knee.
final_note: You learned how the Homestead Act, railroads and Plains Wars destroyed the old way of life on the Plains.

concepts.def: 1862 law giving 160 acres free to settlers
1869 rail link from East to West coasts
Homesteader home built from cut prairie turf
Long trail moving cattle north to railheads
1890 massacre that ended Plains Indian resistance

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Homestead Act of 1862 gave 160 acres of land to any settler who farmed it for 5 years.

Tens of thousands took the offer. On the treeless Plains they built sod houses from cut turf. Many failed — drought, locusts and prairie fires were brutal.

The Transcontinental Railroad was finished in 1869 at Promontory Point, Utah.

It cut journeys from months to days. Cattle barons drove herds north to railheads like Abilene. Buffalo were shot in millions — destroying the Plains Indian economy.

The Plains Wars peaked with Custer's defeat at Little Bighorn in 1876.

But the army hunted Sioux and Cheyenne onto reservations. The massacre of around 250 Sioux at Wounded Knee in December 1890 ended armed resistance forever.
